newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 4.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:

* AT&T shares fell 7.5 percent after the company presented plans that included spending up to $9 billion this year to expand its network and reach new markets, a move that the company said would hurt short-term earnings but is meant to achieve major earnings gains in five years.
* The Conrail board approved a plan to sell the railroad for $10.5 billion, or $115 a share, and to split Conrail's network of railroads.
* Changes made by accounting rule-makers are expected to boost the earnings per share of many companies and reduce price/earnings ratios.
* Concerns about inflation rose after the National Association of Purchasing Manufacturers said manufacturing strength is rising.
* General Motors and Chrysler said their U.S. sales fell in February, but Honda and Nissan reported sizeable gains.

* Some industry experts say oil prices could begin rising again, and economists say prices for the longer term will be buoyed by a capacity shortage among certain companies that supply equipment to oil companies.
* Pearson Plc's Penguin USA, which took $163 million in pretax charges on discounts for retailers, is being criticized for not offering discounts equitably to independent booksellers.
* Tele-Communications said it might seek new financial partners or create joint ventures with other cable operators in an effort to cut debt.
* Apple agreed to settle false advertising charges by the Federal Trade Commission by offering consumers either a rebate or a discount on upgrades for three personal computer models.
* The Supreme Court upheld a key part of patent law that makes it easier for patent holders to protect their inventions from similar ideas.
* The Dow industrials rose 41.18 to 6,918.92. Bonds fell and the dollar rose.
* American Express created a unit to persuade banks to issue its charge and credit cards.
* Read-Rite rejected the hostile bid from Applied Magnetics, whose shares rose 12 percent after the news.

* Paging Network ? Yes. Arch Communications Group ? Yes. And Mtel, or Mobile Telecommunication Technologies ? That one is considered a tough call, even though Bill Gates's Microsoft is still backing it.

"Picking the survivors" is the game some Wall Streeters are now playing with paging companies, whose promises of two-way beepers and Internet-linked pagers once made them among the hottest communications groups around. -- Heard on the Street.
* Bond prices continued to slide on fears that sufficient evidence is building to encourage the Federal Reserve Board to raise interest rates, perhaps as early as this month. -- Credit Markets.
